name: Hot sauce and chili sauces
native_basis_label: sauce as placed on the market (as-consumed liquid)
scope_note: Covers hot sauces and chili sauces. Routed here (not Cat 32 Condiments) because their lead and chromium are chili-borne, the same lead-chromate adulteration platform as turmeric. Contaminant limits bind the finished-sauce (liquid, as-consumed) sovereign limits; total chromium and Cr-VI are adulteration screens. Soy sauce and fish sauce route to Cat 32.

MeHg.rationale: Methylmercury is the organomercury speciation of mercury and is arithmetically bounded by total mercury (MeHg <= tHg); a chili/vinegar/water sauce carries no mercury source and no methylmercury formation pathway, and it is bounded by the total-mercury sauce limit.
MeHg.regulatory_basis: Bounded by the total-Hg sauce standard (Vietnam, 50 ug/kg); no methylmercury sauce ML anywhere

Ni.rationale: No jurisdiction sets a nickel maximum level for sauces. Screened rather than assigned an invented number.
Ni.reference_method: Total-nickel screen (ICP-MS); no sovereign sauce nickel ML.
Ni.trigger: periodic nickel screen; flag on anomalous elevation

Sn.rationale: Hot/chili sauces are sold in glass or plastic bottles, not tinplate cans, so there is no tin source or migration route. Material only for tin-plated canned product.
Sn.reference_method: Packaging control (non-tinplate); periodic ICP-MS tin verification.
Sn.regulatory_basis: No non-canned sauce tin ML; canned-food 250 mg/kg limit is can-only

Al.rationale: Confirmed no-ML (standards-no-ml-confirmed.csv): no government sets an aluminium contaminant maximum level for sauces in any checked jurisdiction (EU 2023/915 lists no Al; Codex; FSANZ; JECFA/EFSA TWI). Aluminium in a chili/vinegar/water sauce is chili-borne background plus any permitted additive; dietary aluminium is managed by weekly intake against the EFSA/JECFA TWI, not by a per-food maximum level, so aluminium is screened rather than aligned to a sovereign number. A sauce is not an accumulating crop, so the spice/bouillon natural-accumulator basis does not apply; this is a material-but-unregulated cell (literature-baseline governs), not a not-material claim.
Al.reference_method: Total-aluminium screen (ICP-MS); managed by intake vs the EFSA/JECFA TWI; no per-food contaminant ML to align to.
Al.trigger: periodic aluminium screen; flag on anomalous elevation

Cr.rationale: No jurisdiction sets a total-chromium food maximum level. As with turmeric, chili-borne lead-chromate adulteration is the material chromium pathway for a chili sauce, so total chromium is screened and co-read with lead as an adulteration co-marker.
Cr.reference_method: Total-chromium screen (ICP-MS), co-read with lead; substrate for reflex Cr-VI speciation.
Cr.trigger: flag when total chromium is elevated and co-occurs with elevated lead (lead-chromate adulteration signature)

Cr-VI.rationale: Lead chromate (a hexavalent-chromium compound) used to adulterate chili is the material Cr-VI pathway for a chili sauce, so Cr-VI is screened, not dismissed. Reflex Cr-VI speciation confirms the chromate where the lead/total-chromium adulteration screen is elevated. No sovereign Cr-VI food ML exists.
Cr-VI.reference_method: Reflex Cr-VI speciation on the lead-chromate adulteration signature.
Cr-VI.trigger: reflex Cr-VI speciation on the lead-chromate adulteration signature

method: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit default; explicit-id lookup; legislated product-form splits preserved; dried-spice basis discipline)
